changelog.change: Demoted from error to warning after the validation run of 2026-09-01. Google Play grants this permission with an approved declaration, and three published apps hold one. The finding still asks the developer to confirm the declaration.

description: QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES is a restricted permission. Google Play accepts it only for a small set of app types, such as a device search app, an antivirus app, or a file manager. An app that declares it without an approved use is removed.

remediation.summary: Remove QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES and declare the specific packages in a <queries> element instead.

title: The app declares QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES

changelog.change: Demoted from error to warning after the validation run of 2026-09-01. Google Play grants this permission with an approved declaration, and three published apps hold one. The finding still asks the developer to confirm the declaration.

description: MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE grants broad access to shared storage. Google Play accepts it only for an app whose core function needs it, such as a file manager or a backup app. Every other app must use the Storage Access Framework or scoped storage.

remediation.summary: Replace the permission with scoped storage or with the Storage Access Framework.

title: The app declares MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE

changelog.change: Gated on the absence of an SMS_DELIVER receiver, which is the default handler shape. The rule carried no precondition at all. The key path was checked against the parser before the rule changed. This does not explain the 6 findings on Kai 9000 and PlainApp: neither declares an SMS_DELIVER receiver, requests ROLE_SMS, or asks to be the default dialer. The rule reads both correctly, and the approved exception Google grants is not visible in code.

description: Google Play restricts the SMS and call log permission group to an app that is the default handler for that function, or to an app with an approved exception. An app that declares one of these permissions without qualifying is refused. A receiver with an SMS_DELIVER intent filter is the default handler shape, so this rule reads the manifest and stays quiet for one. It cannot see an approved exception, which is a grant Google makes outside the code.

remediation.summary: Remove the permission, or apply for a Play Console permissions declaration and set the app as the default handler.

title: The app declares a restricted SMS or call log permission

description: Detect whether the manifest declares READ_MEDIA_IMAGES or READ_MEDIA_VIDEO permissions, which require justification and a Play Console declaration under Google Play policy.

examples: Remove READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/VIDEO from AndroidManifest.xml if not essential.

changelog.change: Compiled from google-play-permissions section Body Sensor Permissions at document version 20260901T173559676Z-52ba10f1. Model confidence 0.45. Awaiting human review.
Verification graded this rule overreach. It added 1 precondition(s), because the policy governs a kind of app and the rule did not say so.

Verification graded this rule wrong_detection and named no fix that a pass can apply. A person must read it. Change the precondition to check that targetSdkVersion is numerically >= 36 (or whatever API level corresponds to Android 16), not just that the key exists.
Verification graded this rule and named a fix that no pass could apply. Corrected by hand: the precondition asked whether targetSdkVersion exists, not what it is.
Writing a rejection case showed the rule could not fire on the fault it names: the check reported an app that declares no permission at all.

Verification graded this rule wrong_detection and named no fix that a pass can apply. A person must read it. Change the manifest check to match_equals 'android.permission.BODY_SENSORS' (i.e., flag when BODY_SENSORS is present) rather than not_equals.
Promoted. Verification graded it accurate, and it raises no error finding on any of the published apps that ran it.

description: Apps targeting Android 16 or higher must not rely on the legacy android.permission.BODY_SENSORS permission for accessing specific health data types; they must use the granular android.permission.health.* permissions instead.

interpretations.interpretation: Presence of BODY_SENSORS permission alongside a target SDK of 36 or higher indicates the app has not migrated to granular health permissions

remediation.summary: Replace the general BODY_SENSORS permission with the specific android.permission.health.* permission that matches the data type accessed (e.g., READ_HEART_RATE, READ_OXYGEN_SATURATION, READ_SKIN_TEMPERATURE) when targeting Android 16 or higher.

title: Migrate BODY_SENSORS to granular health permissions on Android 16+

Verification graded this rule wrong_detection and named no fix that a pass can apply. A person must read it. Precondition should be check_passes on manifest containing ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permission; violation detection should be check_fails on manifest containing ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION permission (i.e., flag when COARSE_LOCATION is missing while FINE_LOCATION is present).
Promoted. Verification graded it accurate, and it raises no error finding on any of the published apps that ran it.

description: Any app requesting ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION must also request ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION to support users who choose to grant only approximate location.

remediation.summary: Add a uses-permission entry for ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION whenever ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is declared.
